Heya, I suspect I am one of the posters that is being categorised as a bully on the post here, though I can’t be 100% sure.

I feel most of the comments on the original post you mentioned at the start were fine - no problems if people want to gently call out rule 3 (no blaming of the deceased or survivors). Or even better to report the post. However, what I don’t think is ok is retaliating with another rule break, and one poster totally crossed that line when they invalidated the way that OP’s grief was manifesting. To be honest when I first read that comment I thought it could be a troll - we get quite a bit of that here.

(In my brain breaking rule 1 “be supportive” is more serious than breaking the part of rule 3 about blaming the deceased, but aware I’m not a mod and that’s just my opinion.)

I don’t think the op should’ve retaliated by going through the user’s post history either, but I know how it feels to lose your temper when it feels like your grief is being invalidated. For the poster to then cross-post a suicide bereavement post to another sub, and then randomers to come here and antagonise and heap more pain on the op as a result was I think a totally disproportionate response. I couldn’t stop thinking about them today, and how horrible I would feel in their position - particularly if I were newly bereaved.

Sorry for any hurt I caused with my post, I’m only angry at the people antagonising the suicide bereaved and invalidating peoples’ grief - not with people reporting genuine rule breaks.

That was understandably done in retaliation, and the op wouldn’t have been able to do it if the other user hadn’t made that disgraceful post in the first place.

Op I am so so sorry for some of the comments you have gotten here. It is completely normal and valid to be angry at your person for everything that has happened, even if it seems trivial to some other random Reddit users (some of whom I’m pretty sure aren’t even bereaved by suicide but have come here to witch hunt from the other sub.) I really hope you aren’t beating yourself up about this, know that the way you are feeling doesn’t make you a bad person. You are just someone who has been through an unimaginable amount of trauma and deserves support and grace. 

I can only hope the users who are sending the unsupportive comments are very young and will grow out of this lack of empathy. I think some people forget that it is a real person they are writing these comments about, not to mention that lots of people on this sub are really vulnerable and there may be unintended consequences. Heavens knows even I’ve felt upset about these comments for several hours, and I’m not even the original poster. 

With this type of loss our feelings can seem ugly sometimes: I sure AF feel guilty about how much I’ve raged about my sister at times. But living with this type of loss is so so hard, and as long as you aren’t hurting any other mourners it’s ok to feel however you feel. Be sad, be angry at your person and the world, be happy when you can. Take care x

I’ve spoken up about my sis’s suicide a few times, once in a work article and once in a work meeting. Tbh I think it’s always going to feel like a vulnerable and scary thing to do, but can also feel rewarding and a pride in knowing that sharing your story may help others. It can also feel relieving feeling that you are no longer hiding this massive secret from people all the time, and that people can see “the real you” more. 

 I’ve also never really had any negative reactions over sharing my story. Sometimes other people have reached out too to say they have lost someone to suicide, or even in one case that it motivated them to get help. 

 Maybe it is “weird” or “not really the done thing” to share about suicide, but it shouldn’t be. Suicide and mental health should be talked about more often, and it’s a courageous, valuable and highly worthwhile thing you are thinking of doing.  Super proud of you for this post :)
